topics: 🍷 Reclining and Wine — Rav vs. Rabbi Yoḥanan: does one blessing on wine cover the whole group?
🍽️ Order of a Meal — the Tosefta's sequence: waiting hall, one hand, wine, then reclining and both hands
🗣️ Ben Zoma's Reason — wine during the meal gets individual blessings because 'the throat is not free'
🧼 Who Leads Grace? — the one who washed first after the meal; Rabbi tells Rav to wash his hands
🌿 Blessings on Scents — incense, musk, balsam oil, jasmine, daffodils, violets, citron
🔥 Oil, Myrtle, and Wine — Beit Shammai, Beit Hillel, and Rabban Gamliel's decision; better the furnace than shaming a friend
🧑‍🎓 Six Disgraces — conduct unbecoming a Torah scholar, from perfume to posture

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Wine at the Table and Blessings on Fragrance
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 43a–43b
overview.hebrewSource: כֹּל הַנְּשָׁמָה תְּהַלֵּל יָהּ — אֵיזֶהוּ דָּבָר שֶׁהַנְּשָׁמָה נֶהֱנֵית מִמֶּנּוּ וְאֵין הַגּוּף נֶהֱנֶה מִמֶּנּוּ? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה הָרֵיחַ
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens at the moment Rav's students learn of his death and fear they never learned the laws of Grace after Meals; an elder resolves their question. The Gemara then asks whether reclining lets one person bless wine for everyone (Rav vs. Rabbi Yoḥanan), walks through the Tosefta's order of a formal meal, and explains with Ben Zoma why wine during the meal gets individual blessings. From the blessing on incense it moves to a catalogue of blessings over scents, the verse that grounds them, and a cluster of Rav Zutra bar Toviya's teachings: torches and demons, and the famous rule that one should rather enter a furnace than shame another in public. It closes with the disputes over oil, myrtle, and wine, and the six things that disgrace a Torah scholar.

slides.title: 🍷 Does Wine Need Reclining? Rav vs. Rabbi Yoḥanan
slides.subtitle: The mishna: 'If they reclined, one blesses for all.' Is that only for bread?

lines.speaker: Rav
lines.text: The mishna speaks only of bread, which requires reclining for one to bless on behalf of all. Wine does not require reclining.

lines.speaker: Rav (v. 2)
lines.text: Some say Rav meant: reclining is effective only for bread. For wine, reclining does not help; each drinker blesses for himself.

lines.speaker: R' Yoḥanan
lines.text: Even for wine, reclining is effective.

lines.speaker: Objection
lines.text: The Tosefta: before the meal the guests drink wine and each blesses for himself; once reclined, wine comes and one blesses for all. Version 1 of Rav is contradicted by the first clause; version 2 by the last.

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: Version 1: guests in the hall are different, since their mind is on leaving (דְּדַעְתַּיְיהוּ לְמִיעְקַר). Version 2: once reclining works for the bread, it works for the wine too (מִגּוֹ).

callout.label: Backdrop:
callout.text: The daf begins with Rav's students tearing their garments a second time: 'Rav is dead, and we have not learned the halakhot of Grace after Meals.' An elder resolved their question: once diners say 'let us go and eat in such-and-such a place', it is as if they reclined.

slides.title: 🍽️ The Order of a Formal Meal (Tosefta)
slides.subtitle: Two rooms, two washings, two rounds of wine

steps.content: 1️⃣ Guests enter and sit on benches and chairs (קָתֶדְרָאוֹת) until everyone has arrived
2️⃣ Water is brought; each washes one hand, to hold the cup
3️⃣ Wine is served; each blesses for himself
4️⃣ They go up and recline; water is brought again and each washes both hands
5️⃣ Wine during the meal: one blesses for all (Tosefta) — though our mishna says each blesses for himself during the meal
6️⃣ Ben Zoma explains the mishna: during the meal each blesses for himself because אֵין בֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה פָּנוּי — the throat is not free; after the meal, one blesses for all

callout.label: And the incense:
callout.text: The one who blessed on the wine also blesses on the incense (mugmar) after the meal. Why him? Because he washed his hands first after the meal. This supports Rav: whoever washes first at the end is designated to lead Grace. Hence Rabbi told Rav 'stand and wash your hands' — and Rabbi Ḥiyya reassured the trembling Rav: 'Son of noblemen, he is telling you to review Grace after Meals.'

slides.title: 🌿 Which Blessing for Which Scent?
slides.subtitle: Rava bar Yirmeya: bless incense when its column of smoke rises, just as HaMotzi is said before eating, when one intends to smell
rows: Rav Ḥisda in Rav's (or Ze'iri's) name — but a baraita limiting 'fragrant trees' to balsam of Rabbi's house, balsam of Caesar, and myrtle refutes this (תְּיוּבְתָּא)
It comes from a living creature, not a tree
בּוֹרֵא שֶׁמֶן אַרְצֵנוּ / בּוֹרֵא שֶׁמֶן עָרֵב
Rav Yehuda, who loved Eretz Yisrael, said 'oil of our land'; Rabbi Yoḥanan: 'pleasant oil' for everyone else
Costus; oil pressed or ground with spices
Rav Adda bar Ahava: costus only; Rav Kahana: even pressed oil; Neharde'a: even ground oil
Mar Zutra's proof that soft stalks are 'trees': 'hidden under the trees of flax' (Joshua 2:6)
Rav Yehuda: '…and created in it beautiful creatures and trees for people to enjoy'

callout.label: Why bless a smell at all?
callout.text: Rav Zutra bar Toviya in Rav's name: 'Let every soul praise the Lord' (Psalms 150:6). What does the soul enjoy but not the body? Scent. Rav also taught that the young men of Israel will one day give off fragrance like Lebanon (Hosea 14:7).

slides.title: 🔥 Oil, Myrtle, and Wine: Which Comes First?
slides.subtitle: Two baraitot on the order of blessings, and Rabban Gamliel's tie-break

boxes.title: Beit Shammai
items: Oil and myrtle: bless the oil first, then the myrtle
Oil and wine: hold oil in the right hand, wine in the left; bless oil, then wine

boxes.title: Beit Hillel
items: Oil and myrtle: bless the myrtle first, then the oil
Oil and wine: wine in the right hand, oil in the left; bless wine, then oil
Then wipe the oil on the servant's head — or on the wall if the servant is a Torah scholar, since it is disgraceful for a scholar to go out perfumed

boxes.title: Rabban Gamliel decides
items: Oil — we enjoy its scent and its anointing; myrtle — scent only
Rabbi Yoḥanan: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הַמַּכְרִיעַ, the halakha follows the decisor

callout.label: Rav Pappa's dodge:
callout.text: At Rav Huna son of Rav Ika's house, Rav Pappa blessed the myrtle first. Challenged, he claimed Rava ruled like Beit Hillel. The Gemara says it was not so; he said it only to extricate himself. Fittingly, this amud also teaches: better to throw oneself into a fiery furnace than to shame another in public — learned from Tamar, who did not expose Judah (Genesis 38:25).

slides.title: 🧑‍🎓 Six Things That Disgrace a Torah Scholar
slides.subtitle: A baraita, with the Gemara's limits on each
rows: Going out perfumed to the market
Only where people are suspected of homosexuality (Rabbi Yoḥanan); only on clothing, not on the body, since sweat removes it (Rav Sheshet); hair is like clothing — or like the body (Rav Pappa)
Because of suspicion — but not if he has a set time to study, since everyone knows where he is going
Only a patch on a patch, on the upper, on the road, in summer (Mar Zutra son of Rav Naḥman, explaining why Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba himself did so)
Conversing with a woman in the market
Even his wife, daughter, or sister — not everyone knows his relatives (Rav Ḥisda)
Reclining at a meal with ignoramuses
Lest he be drawn after them
They will call him negligent (פּוֹשֵׁעַ)
A long stride takes 1/500 of one's eyesight; remedy: the kiddush wine of Shabbat eve
Even four cubits — as if pushing away the feet of the Shekhina, 'the whole earth is full of His glory' (Isaiah 6:3)

callout.label: Also from Rav:
callout.text: A torch on a dark road is like two people (including the bearer), moonlight like three — for a demon is seen and harms one, is seen but harmless to two, and is not seen at all by three.

summary.principle: At a shared meal, reclining together turns individual blessings into one; and just as the body's pleasures require blessings, so does the soul's pleasure in scent — 'let every soul praise the Lord'.

flowSteps.content: 🍷 Mishna: 'if they reclined, one blesses for all' — Rav: bread only; Rabbi Yoḥanan: wine too
🍽️ Tosefta order: hall → one hand → wine (each blesses) → recline → both hands → wine (one blesses). Ben Zoma: during the meal the throat is not free

columns.content: 🧼 Whoever washes first after the meal leads Grace and blesses the incense
🌿 Scents: trees → עצי בשמים; herbs → עשבי בשמים; musk → מיני בשמים; fruit → שנתן ריח טוב

flowSteps.content: 🔥 Oil before myrtle (Rabban Gamliel decides; halakha follows the decisor); rather the furnace than shaming another (Tamar)
🎓 Key Principle: A scholar's dignity is public property — six (or eight) things disgrace him, each bounded by the Gemara to real suspicion

quiz.q: According to the first version of Rav's statement, for which food does reclining allow one person to bless on behalf of all?
o: Bread only; wine does not require reclining
Wine only; bread never needs reclining
Both bread and wine equally
Neither; each person always blesses for himself
quiz.e: Rav limits the mishna's 'if they reclined, one blesses for all' to bread. Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that even wine requires reclining.

quiz.q: Why, according to Ben Zoma, does each diner bless for himself when wine is served during the meal?
o: Because wine during the meal is not considered important
Because the throat is not free — diners are busy eating and cannot all be ready to drink together
Because reclining has not yet begun
Because wine during a meal is secondary to the bread
quiz.e: Ben Zoma explained: 'since the throat is not free' (אֵין בֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה פָּנוּי). After the meal, when all are free, one blesses for everyone.

quiz.q: Which blessing is recited over musk, and why?
o: 'Who creates fragrant trees', because it is treated like incense
'Who creates fragrant plants', because it grows in the field
'Who creates various spices', because it comes from a living creature
'Who gave pleasant fragrance in fruits', because it is sweet
quiz.e: Rav Ḥisda's teaching: all incense gets 'fragrant trees' except musk, which is from a living creature, so its blessing is 'Who creates various spices' (בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי בְשָׂמִים).

quiz.q: When oil and myrtle are brought together, how does Rabban Gamliel decide, and what is the halakha?
o: Myrtle first, since it is a plant; the halakha follows Beit Hillel
Oil first, since we enjoy both its scent and its anointing; Rabbi Yoḥanan rules that the halakha follows the decisor
Either order, since both are fragrances
Wine first, then oil, then myrtle
quiz.e: Rabban Gamliel sided with Beit Shammai because oil gives two benefits, scent and anointing, while myrtle gives only scent. Rabbi Yoḥanan: the halakha follows the decisor.

quiz.q: From whom does the Gemara derive that one should rather throw himself into a fiery furnace than shame another in public?
o: From Tamar, who did not expose Judah when she was brought out to be burned
From Rav, who trembled when Rabbi told him to wash his hands
From Rav Pappa, who blessed the myrtle first
From the Torah scholar who may not go out perfumed
quiz.e: The teaching is derived from Tamar (Genesis 38:25): facing execution, she sent Judah the pledges and let him identify them rather than humiliate him publicly.
